subject: Dedicated renewal — throughput/headroom & autoscale latency adjustments
messages:
From: Sierra Holt <sierra@auroraai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@auroraai.com>
Date: 2027-05-01T18:12:00-07:00
Subject: Renewal conversation — capacity headroom question

Hi Monica,

Our renewal for Dedicated capacity is coming up at the end of May and the product team wants to lock in more headroom for live traffic spikes. Right now we run 12 A100 GPUs reserved; we're seeing a regular daily burst that taxes our warm-up time and incurs throttles.

Two asks that would help us decide quickly:
- Can Redwood commit to a short scale-up latency (e.g., p95 < 15s) for cold-to-warm bursts?
- Is it possible to add a small reserved warm pool (2–4 GPU equiv) that is billed at a lower utilization rate but kept pre-warmed?

We're also evaluating pricing implications if we increase our min replicas or add reserved headroom. Procurement is copied.

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if it's easier.

Sierra Holt
Head of Platform
Aurora AI

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Sierra Holt <sierra@auroraai.com>
Cc: Procurement <procure@auroraai.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity headroom question

Hi Sierra —

Thanks for the clear ask, and congrats on the growth — this is exactly the sort of scenario Dedicated is designed for. We've sketched a renewal amendment that balances throughput guarantees with cost predictability; I attached a draft for your review (20270504-Aurora-dedicated-amendment-draft.pdf) and included last quarter's usage for context. High level proposal: 

- Reserved capacity: increase committed GPUs from 12 -> 20 (add 8 A100-equivalent GPUs).
- Warm pool: reserve a 2-GPU warm pool (kept pre-warmed for your model family) with a reduced billing tier (50% of a reserved GPU rate while idle).
- Autoscale min/max: move min replicas from 4 -> 6 and max replicas from 20 -> 28 to give headroom while limiting spend.
- Scale-up latency SLO: commit to p90 scale-up to ready < 10s, p95 < 18s (applies when warm pool available; fallback p95 < 30s on pure cold starts).
- Throughput assurance: we can guarantee sustained per-GPU throughput at the same profile you saw in Q1; if average throughput per-GPU drops below 90% of baseline for three consecutive days, we'll provide credits and an adjustment plan.

Pricing impact is included in the draft. If that looks directionally right, I'll loop in Marissa (quote/discount approvals) and Karthik (technical SLO wording). If you want to tweak warm pool size or the min/max, say the word and we'll run the billing sensitivity.

Available for a 30m call today or tomorrow morning.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive — North America
Redwood Inference

Attachment: 20270504-Aurora-dedicated-amendment-draft.pdf
From: Procurement <procure@auroraai.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>, Sierra Holt <sierra@auroraai.com>
Date: 2027-05-02T11:35:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity headroom question

Monica,

Thanks — the draft looks reasonable at a glance. Two procurement items before we proceed to signature:
1) Clarify billing for the warm pool when it is utilized vs idle (how are partial-hour spikes billed?).
2) Need explicit language about credits and remediation steps if the scale-up SLO is missed during a declared incident window.

If you can put those lines into the amendment, we can try to accelerate.

—Procurement (Aurora AI)

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>
To: Procurement <procure@auroraai.com>, Sierra Holt <sierra@auroraai.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T08:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity headroom question

Thanks for the flag — copied Marissa and Karthik to confirm the billing and credit language. Quick answers before they chime in: 

- Warm-pool billing: idle warm pool billed at 50% of a reserved GPU hourly rate; when a warm GPU is taken to serve traffic we bill the delta to full reserved rate for that hour. For very short spikes (< 1 minute) we have a per-minute smoothing policy (no retroactive full-hour charge) — I'll put precise numbers in the amendment.
- Credits: we propose a tiered credit band tied to p95 miss severity and duration; remediation includes priority incident review and a runbook for pre-warm tuning.

Marissa — can you confirm discount/term implications if they accept a 20-GPU commit? Karthik — small ask to confirm the SLO wording (p90/p95 numbers) and note any caveats around model family or sequence length distributions.

Monica

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.inference.com>
To: Monic­a Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.inference.com>, Procurement <procure@auroraai.com>, Sierra Holt <sierra@auroraai.com>
Date: 2027-05-03T09:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Renewal conversation — capacity headroom question

Hi all — technical quick note from the infra side:

- Warm pool sizing: 2 GPUs should cover typical traffic fractiles for Aurora's QPS pattern but if you have short, very high peaks (1000x baseline) we recommend a 4-GPU warm pool or an additional short-term burst bucket. Happy to run a 7-day simulation if you share the peak traces.
- Scale-up SLO caveat: p95 < 18s is achievable when requests benefit from KV/prefix caching and identical model variants in the warm pool. If your traffic mixes multiple model families or substantially longer sequence lengths (>1024 tokens) p95 can shift toward ~25-30s. We'll add a clause that SLOs apply to the validated model family and typical sequence length range, with a change-control process for additional families.
- Billing note: the per-minute smoothing Monica referenced is applied to spikes under 5 minutes; above that we pro-rate by minute up to the hour.

I'll draft suggested amendment text for the SLO/credit table and upload as part of the PDF.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.inference.com>

Subject: Dedicated renewal — next steps and signature

Sierra — thanks everyone for the quick turn. Action items and next steps: 

1) I'll incorporate Karthik's SLO caveat language and the procurement billing clarifications into the amendment and re-share by end of day.
2) Marissa will confirm the discount band for a 20-GPU commit (Marissa — can you reply with the %-range so we can forward to procurement?).
3) Sierra/procurement — once the final amendment is approved we'll circulate a DocuSign link for signature (attached link below).

DocuSign (pre-auth): https://www.docusign.com/aurora-renewal-2027
HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/4859203
